earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog sources for chig1239 are comparative/classification only (Josserand 1983, Auderset et al. 2023, Smith-Stark); no grammar or phonology of Chigmecatitlan Mixtec located.

sources.citation: Carroll, Lucien. 2015. Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec Word Prosody. PhD, UCSD, Table A.2 (sibling folder mixt1425); Bradley & Josserand 1982 El protomixteco y sus descendientes (sibling folder huit1252)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Carroll lists Chigmecatitlán (Chg/Chig, mii, Baja:N) only as one of Josserand's survey towns; Bradley & Josserand name Santa María Chigmecatitlán only as a border settlement. Nothing variety-specific on stress.

sources.citation: LingMex (COLMEX, Bibliografía lingüística de México desde 1970), simple-search JSON queries 'Chigmecatitlán', 'Chigmecatitlan', 'Tlaltempan', 'suroeste de Puebla'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 0 records for Chigmecatitlán and Tlaltempan; 'suroeste de Puebla' returns 2 unrelated items (Nahua contact history; Tepehuan Spanish). No Mexican linguistic publication on this variety since 1970 is catalogued.

sources.citation: Auderset, Greenhill, DiCanio & Campbell. 2023. Subgrouping in a 'dialect continuum'. J. Language Evolution 8(1): 33-63 (text already held by the project in sibling folder apas1235) and Auderset MixteCoDB coding details (sibling folder sind1277)

sources.note: Chigmecatitlán data = Josserand 1983 wordlist only (MixteCoDB row chig11, chig1239, mii); placed in Subgroup 7.4.1 Northern Baja with Tlaltempan and San Jerónimo Xayacatlán. No stress statement.

sources.note: Autonym Da'an davi; Tlaltempan + Chigmecatitlán; 1,350 (2010 INEGI); 'None known. 23% intelligibility of Chazumba.. Low intelligibility with all Mixtec; very different.' Latin script; no literature. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Josserand, J. Kathryn. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History (Proto-Mixtec and Modern Mixtec Text). PhD dissertation, Tulane University, xv+711 pp. (UMI 8400802)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only work with primary Chigmecatitlán and Tlaltempan data (survey wordlists, codes Chig/Tlal); p. 180 defines the Mixtec couplet with stress on its first syllable; the wordlist appendix may carry variety-level phonological notes. Best available, but comparative, not a description of this variety.

sources.note: Not accessible (ProQuest only, no open copy). Secondary quotations (Carroll 2015: 86; Penner 2019: 91-92, held by the project) report Josserand 1983: 180 defining the Mixtec couplet as 'composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two' -- a pan-Mixtec/Proto-Mixtec claim, not a Chigmecatitlán statement.
